mighty-mulloway.name: Mighty Mulloway Sculpture
mighty-mulloway.bio: Bronze mulloway sculpture by Ken Martin, unveiled in 2026 at the Y-Stop roadhouse in Yalata on the Eyre Highway.

notes.pin: Y-Stop Yalata Roadhouse, Eyre Highway, Yalata (OSM roadhouse node); sculpture stands at the roadhouse.
notes.other: Unveiled 16 July 2026 per Yalata community page; very new.

neptune-islands.name: Neptune Islands
neptune-islands.bio: Remote islands off Port Lincoln, reached by boat, where operators run great white shark cage dives.
neptune-islands.ticket_note: Sold by several operators (Calypso Star Charters, Rodney Fox Shark Expeditions), so no single official site.

notes.pin: Wikipedia coordinates for the island group; boat-only, no visitor point on land.
notes.other: One-day cage-dive trip from Port Lincoln about 12 h with ~3 h each way; a Visitor Use Fee (~$45) for the marine park is added by operators. Draft hours 4-8 changed to the day-trip length.

greenly-beach.name: Greenly Beach
greenly-beach.bio: Surf and swimming beach at Coulta, an hour from Port Lincoln, with bluffs, reef and tall dunes behind.
greenly-beach.ticket_note: No single steward; free open beach.

notes.pin: Greenly Beach Road, Coulta (end of access road at the southern end of the beach); OSM natural=beach or Wikipedia article Greenly Beach.
notes.other: Address Coulta 5607, Lower Eyre Peninsula council area; re-home if the pin falls inside Port Lincoln or Coffin Bay span.

googs-track.name: Googs Track
googs-track.bio: A 4WD track through Yumbarra and Yellabinna, crossing the dingo fence and dunes to Goog's Lake north of Ceduna.

notes.pin: Midpoint of the whole track (OSM route); Goog's Lake at the northern end, track starts about 30 km north of Ceduna.
notes.other: Track and campsites closed 1 Dec 2026 to 28 Feb 2027 (annual summer closure, reopens 1 Mar 2027). Park page lists only camping fee ($15.40/night); no entry fee or permit shown. 4WD; travel south to north recommended.

fowlers-bay.name: Fowlers Bay Conservation Park
fowlers-bay.bio: Giant sand dunes beside Fowlers Bay, with sea lions, wombats and seabirds, and fishing for salmon and mulloway.

notes.pin: Wikipedia park coordinates (centroid); use the dunes access or Fowlers Bay jetty/village point instead.
notes.other: Park page lists only a camping fee ($15.40/night); no entry fee. Dogs not permitted. Bio omits Scotts Beach/Mexican Hat (draft source, not rechecked).

head-of-bight.name: Head of Bight
head-of-bight.bio: Clifftop boardwalks at Head of Bight where southern right whales calve in the water below, from about June to October.

notes.pin: Head of Bight Whale Watching Centre / lookout carpark, Yalata (Wikipedia point is the bight).
notes.other: Adult $20 whale season, $10 off season (centre price list). Centre open all week; seasonal hours. Run by Yalata community (Aboriginal Lands Trust land).

bunda-cliffs.name: Bunda Cliffs
bunda-cliffs.bio: Sea cliffs up to 120 m high running more than 200 km along the Nullarbor coast, with three signposted lookouts.
bunda-cliffs.ticket_note: Free roadside lookouts inside Nullarbor National Park; no separate steward page.

notes.pin: One of the three official Bunda Cliffs lookouts off the Eyre Highway (OSM tourism=viewpoint); Wikipedia point is the cliff line.
notes.other: Camping along the cliffs not permitted (unstable edge).

nullarbor-national-park.name: Nullarbor National Park
nullarbor-national-park.bio: Flat karst plain where sinkholes open into caves, with sea cliffs on the coast and wombats among its wildlife.

notes.pin: Wikipedia centroid; use a visitor point such as the Murrawijinnie Caves or Koonalda Homestead access, not the centroid, and not Bunda Cliffs or Head of Bight pins.
notes.other: Page title "Nullarbor..." (covers national park, wilderness protection area, regional reserve); fees only for camping ($15.40/night). Murrawijinnie Caves are the only caves open to the public. Park is about 300 km west of Ceduna.

eyre-highway.name: Eyre Highway
eyre-highway.bio: The road across the Nullarbor from Ceduna to the Western Australian border, with lookouts and roadhouses along the way.
eyre-highway.ticket_note: Public road with no single steward.

notes.pin: Midpoint of the SA stretch (Ceduna to the border, ~480 km): near Nullarbor Roadhouse area; take from OSM route relation.

big-galah.name: Big Galah
big-galah.bio: A large pink galah sculpture at Kimba, beside the sign marking the halfway point across Australia.
big-galah.ticket_note: Roadside sculpture with no official site beyond the council tourist page (blocked to scripts).

notes.pin: Eyre Highway, Kimba (OSM tourism=artwork or attraction "Big Galah"); Wikipedia article Big Galah.

kimba-museum.name: Kimba Museum
kimba-museum.bio: Museum with a 1908 Pioneer House, one-teacher school, pioneer store and tractor collection, open mid-week.
kimba-museum.ticket_note: Official site is the Kimba council tourist page (403 to scripts), see needs_browser; no URL linked until verified.

notes.pin: 15307 Eyre Highway, Kimba, opposite the grain silos (OSM museum node).
notes.other: Listing says Wednesdays and Thursdays (hours Wed-Fri 9-2) or by appointment; "from $5" is the lowest listed price, adult price not confirmed.

lake-gilles.name: Lake Gilles Conservation Park
lake-gilles.bio: Saline lake with gypsum dunes and mallee scrub, crossed by the Eyre Highway, with birdlife to watch.

notes.pin: Wikipedia centroid; use the lake access off Eyre Highway (2WD) instead.
notes.other: Free entry per park page. Closed on days of Catastrophic Fire Danger. Northern area near the lake is 4WD only. Draft said "walking trails": not on park page, dropped.
